{{Top|leg|italics=1}}
{{Quote|Te racin ka'ra juaan kote.|From the war chant, ''[[Kote Darasuum]]''|<ref name="Star Wars: Republic Commando">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>}}
The '''''Ka'ra''''' were an ancient [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] myth. In times long past,<ref name="Mando'a">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}</ref> when the Mandalorians were a devoutly [[Mandalorian religion|religious]] people, they believed the [[Star/Legends|stars]] in the night sky over [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] to be the spirits of the [[Death/Legends|fallen]] [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|rulers]] of their cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> According to myth, the ''Ka'ra'' represented a guiding council that the culture's former leaders would join upon their deaths.<ref name="Mando'a" />

Over [[Time/Legends|time]], the Mandalorians eventually developed into a more secular and less superstitious society. These more pragmatic and rational Mandalorians no longer looked upon the myths of the past as literal examples of the supernatural, but instead as parables. From ancient stories such as the ''Ka'ra'' and the ''[[Akaanati'kar'oya]]'', they sought allegorical or philosophical insights, rather than factual truth.<ref name="TMPaC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Ka'ra'' were first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe in the [[Star Wars Insider]] article, ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Karen Traviss]] and published in [[February]] [[2006]] as part of the magazine's [[Star Wars Insider 86|eighty-sixth]] issue.
